significance: A gurdwara built beside a spring within the walls of Rohtas Fort in Jhelum district, marking a place associated with Guru Nanak's travels. An earlier memorial raised by Charat Singh was replaced by the present building, commissioned by Maharaja Ranjit Singh and finished in 1834.
story: Sikh tradition holds that when Bhai Mardana complained of thirst, Guru Nanak struck the ground with his staff and a spring appeared; Sher Shah Suri's engineers are said to have tried three times, and failed, to move the spring up the hill to serve his new fort.
